newsitem.title: USA: Empi recalls some electrotherapy devices.
newsitem.headline: Empi recalls some electrotherapy devices.

text.p: Empi Inc, a medical device manufacturer, said in its electrotherapy sector the company is conducting a voluntary recall of about 900 Dynex IV TENS units due to a quality issue unrelated to patient safety.
The company said sufficient inventory is in place to replace the affected units which are sold by wholesale distributors and dealers. No significant loss of sales revenue is anticipated, Empi said.
During the first quarter, the company reported earnings rose to $0.29 per share from $0.25 and sales gained to $18 million from $16.9 million.
President Joseph Laptewicz said sales in the rehabilitation market segment were up seven percent in the quarter from a year ago.
"Progress was slower in the incontinence segment as revenue slipped six percent due to reduced sales of our clinical sEMG system," Laptewicz said in a statement.
"Growing sales of the Innova PFS product line, the current focus of the incontinence field sales organization, were not enough to compensate for the sEMG weakness," he said.
